prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / precise composition correction. Revise the mobile Habits dashboard to match the FIRST reference image's card composition and spacing extremely closely. Image 1 is the ORIGINAL USER REFERENCE and is the controlling visual/layout specification. Image 2 is our previous concept B and is an EDIT TARGET whose content may be retained, but whose spacing, surfaces, grouping and background were wrong. Do not average the two layouts. Follow image 1 for geometry, padding, corners, backgrounds and visual hierarchy; retain habit-tracking content and valid stats from image 2.
OUTPUT: a single very high fidelity flat portrait app screen, approximately 880x1780 aspect (about 1:2), edge-to-edge app artwork with native status area and home indicator. No physical phone bezel, no surrounding stone tabletop, no presentation labels. The near-black behind the panels IS PART OF THE APP, not a device frame.
EXACT MACRO COMPOSITION from image 1, measured as percentages of the app screen:
- Near-black charcoal #121313 foundation across the full screen, visible as narrow continuous gutters between the main panels. Do NOT use a global white canvas. Do NOT spread everything over one light background.
- TOP WHITE PANEL occupies roughly y=0% to 43.5%, nearly full width, just 4-6px outer inset at 430pt width, large top corners and approximately 18pt rounded bottom corners. This is ONE continuous softly luminous off-white panel containing status bar, header, category pills, the three habit rows, and the small Ajouter pill. No separate card around the list, no inset white-on-white list card.
- A narrow charcoal horizontal gutter, approximately 5-6pt at 430pt screen width.
- MIDDLE ROW occupies roughly y=44% to 66%. Exactly TWO equal-size nearly square cards, pastel pink on left and pale pistachio on right, each about 49.2% of the available width, separated by only a 5-6pt charcoal gutter. Cards are large continuous colored fields and have approximately 24pt rounded corners. They extend nearly to the screen's left/right edges. No 16-24pt page padding or large white gaps.
- Another 5-6pt charcoal horizontal gutter.
- BOTTOM WHITE PANEL occupies roughly y=66.7% to 100%, full width with strongly rounded upper corners. Its upper ~60% is a full-width pale blue hydration card; its lower ~40% is a quiet off-white navigation zone. This bottom region must visually match the original image: blue hydration above, little carousel markers and icon-only bottom navigation below. Preserve visible charcoal around the upper rounded corners.
TOP PANEL INTERNAL LAYOUT, match image 1:
Status time at upper left, dynamic-island shape at upper center if needed, status indicators right, all within safe area. Large rounded black "Habits" at about x=4%, y=8.5%, small pale-yellow rounded chip with orange flame and number "3" at right (not a large "3 jours" banner). Four subtly translucent white category pills in one row below, generous round corners, regular-weight category names and bold stats, with "Sport 60 %", "Esprit 100 %", "Quotidien 0 %", "Alimentation 71 %". Keep category name text no larger than the original.
Three bare list rows with colorful simple glyphs at left, bold title and muted subtitle. "Course à pied" / "3 / 5 km"; "Méditer" / "10 / 10 min"; "Lire" / "1 / 1 séance". Icons are standalone colored pictograms without circular avatar backgrounds. NO separators, NO per-row right buttons or duplicate checks, NO extra nested containers. Keep generous vertical rhythm exactly like image 1. A SMALL floating-looking white rounded "+ Ajouter" pill aligned lower RIGHT inside this upper white panel, with green circle plus, matching original scale. Not a full-width green add button.
MIDDLE CARDS:
Pink left "Progression" large black rounded heading top left; pink circular arrow button top right. Large elegant continuous line/area chart across the middle that reaches the left and right edges of this card, no point-marker dots. At bottom, two balanced columns: "58 %" / "Objectif" and "+6 %" / "vs hier". Muted pink-gray secondary labels. Match the original card's exact generous spacing and typography positions.
Green right "Régularité" black rounded heading and small muted "Cette semaine" below, green circular simple walking/check glyph upper right. A thin horizontal green progress motif across its middle, like the original's activity baseline. At bottom two columns, "3 jours" / "de suite" and "120 XP" / "cumulés". This is existing habit data, no steps/calories/heart-rate claims. Retain the pale-green material, generous spacing, edge-to-edge chart and relative element sizes of the original.
BOTTOM HYDRATION AND NAV:
Pale blue full-width rounded hydration card. At TOP LEFT a tiny horizontal sequence of seven rounded pastel-to-blue squares, then muted label "Hydratation" below. At TOP RIGHT a compact black segmented capsule, blue active "Semaine", white inactive "Mois". NOT a title at giant size, NOT an Aujourd'hui pill.
Bottom LEFT: two simple flat blue bottle silhouettes and three glass shapes at different fill levels, matching the original's placement and scale. Bottom RIGHT: big rounded black "1,5 L", smaller muted blue-gray "75 % de l’objectif". No additional green "+250mL" button that would change the reference geometry.
Below the hydration panel, on the bottom white surface: centered carousel markers, one short amber rounded dash and three small black dots, then a spacious icon-only native tab row. Left selected tab a soft gray rounded pill with a solid black day/habit-stack icon, center black progression/chart icon, right solid black profile icon. No visible word labels and no green selected navigation background. Home indicator at bottom.
FINISH: Match the FIRST image's card geometry, gaps, backdrop, rhythm and quiet glossy rounded native feel as closely as possible. The main correction is black gutters and single grouped upper card, not just recoloring the previous screen. Subtle soft material variation is welcome as in original, but no heavy shadows, no invented extra widgets, no off-white padding separating middle cards. All text in French, readable, all values fictional demonstration data.
